[{"id": "nnvMTG5Sl5", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "🛠️ Operations Manual", "col": 12}}, {"id": "B-CtTCmVDX", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The operations module contains features related to the operation of the church (maintenance, assets, etc).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "w8oEjl0tNc", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "📦Assets", "col": 12}}, {"id": "6IlcMu_Ikb", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Property of the church.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "0J08Yp0qsz", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When adding a new asset, note the following:
- Try to give the asset a short but descriptive title
- Additional details can be added in the 'Notes' field
- The location of the asset can be set (or added) in the \"Location\" field.
- Tick 'Bookable' to let people book the asset with a Room Booking. See Equipment under Room Bookings.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "SxmzzpDQ__", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "📍 Location", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ppmgXY62eA", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A location is any physical or virtual space where something can reside.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Zy36TCqTow", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When adding a new location, note the following:
- Locations can be set as a 'group'. This will allow other locations to be 'grouped' under this location.
- Locations can be linked to an address. When linked, the map moves to the address. An address that is not on the map yet is looked up first, unless 'Look Up Addresses for the Map' is clear in People Settings. Then place the pin by hand.
- Shapes/drawings can be added to the map view for reference purposes (i.e. circle an area in an open space)", "col": 12}}, {"id": "8zFlGyC4XI", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "✅Tasks", "col": 12}}, {"id": "kDsKUF3xl2", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Items that need to be completed. (Like a checklist or todo-list)", "col": 12}}, {"id": "t5oHSN8It-", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When you add a new task, note the following:
1. To add sub-tasks, tick Is Group, then make new tasks and choose the group task in Parent Task.
2. To give a task to a person, use Assign in the sidebar of the task. Only a user who can change the task can assign it, and you can assign only users who can see the church of the task.
3. When you assign an Open task, its status changes to Assigned. The assignment takes the due date of the task. When you change the due date, the open assignments move with it.
4. When you set the status to Completed, all assignments of the task close.
5. The day before a task is due, each person assigned to it gets an email and a desk notification, unless the task is Completed. To change the message or the number of days, open the Church Task Due notification.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "task_work_b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Work orders. A work order is a task for a repair or a job on an asset or a room. Set Type to Work Order. Then the Work Order section shows: Requested By (a person), Asset and Room. Set Priority to Low, Medium, High or Urgent. Only a Church Manager adds work orders. Church Staff can change them. The asset, the room and the person must belong to the church of the task, or be shared with all churches. When you move a task to another church, these links are checked again. The Open Work Orders report lists the work orders that are not Completed, with the earliest due date first. The Work Orders section on an asset or a room shows how many work orders name it. You cannot delete an asset or a room that a task names.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "mm_h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "📝Meeting Minutes", "col": 12}}, {"id": "mm_b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Meeting Minutes record board or committee meetings.
- Optionally link the related Function.
- List who was present in the 'Attendees' table and write the record in the 'Minutes' field.
- Set 'Approved On' once the minutes are approved.
- If the meeting was recorded, attach the audio file in the 'Recording' section. It can be played back from the form.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "room_h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "🚪Rooms", "col": 12}}, {"id": "room_b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A Room is a space that people can book, such as the sanctuary, a classroom or the fellowship hall. Tick Bookable to let people book it. Tick Requires Approval when an approver must approve each booking. Add users to Approvers to choose who approves the bookings of the room. Each approver needs the Church Staff or Church Manager role and access to the church of the room. When Approvers is empty, the Church Managers of the church approve the bookings.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "room_names_b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Each church gives its rooms their own names, so two churches can each have a room called Sanctuary. One church cannot have two rooms with the same name. A shared room is on the list of every church, so its name must be different from every other room. A new room gets an ID such as ROOM-0001, and forms and lists show its name.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "room_setup_b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Setups. Add the ways a room can be set up, such as Banquet or Theatre, in the Setups table of the room. Give each setup its own name, and add the capacity, a description and a photo if you want. On a booking, choose one setup of the room in Setup, and add Setup Notes for the people who set up the room. The list shows only the setups of the chosen room. A booking without a room cannot have a setup. If you remove a setup from a room, the bookings that already use it keep it.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "room_question_b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Questions. To ask each booking of a room some questions, such as the number of guests or the need for sound, choose a Question Set in Question Set on the room. A room can use only a Question Set of your church or a shared one. When you choose the room on a booking, the questions open in a dialog. Click Done to keep the answers on the booking. To change the answers later, click Answer Questions. A booking cannot be saved until each required question has an answer. If you move a booking to a room with other questions, the old answers are removed and you answer the new questions. If you change the Question Set of a room, its bookings keep their old answers until someone answers the new questions with Answer Questions. A blocked time asks no questions.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "roombk_h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "📅Room Bookings", "col": 12}}, {"id": "room_book_b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "To book a room, add a Room Booking. Note the following:
- The Room list shows only rooms with Bookable ticked. A booking of any other room is refused.
- On a room that does not require approval, a new booking is Approved at once. On a room with Requires Approval ticked, a new booking stays Requested until an approver approves it. A booking that an approver of the room makes is Approved at once.
- Each approver gets a ToDo for a Requested booking. An approver opens the booking and clicks Decide, then Approve or Deny. The ToDos close, and the user who made the booking gets an email with the decision.
- If a user who is not an approver changes the room, the start or the end of an approved booking, the booking goes back to Requested and waits for approval again. A change to the notes only keeps it Approved.
- Two bookings of one room cannot overlap. When a booking clashes, the message names the clashing bookings of your churches. It counts the bookings of other churches, but does not name them.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "room_conflict_b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Conflicts. Tick Request Anyway to send a booking that clashes to the approvers. The booking gets the status Conflict, and each approver gets a ToDo. A Conflict booking does not keep other people from booking the room. An approver opens it and clicks Resolve, then one of these:
- Keep This Booking approves it and denies the Requested and Conflict bookings that it clashes with. If an Approved booking still has the room at that time, it is refused.
- Share the Room ticks Can Share Room on it and on each booking that it clashes with, and approves it.
Two bookings that both have Can Share Room ticked do not clash. A recurring Function copies its bookings with Request Anyway ticked, so a copy that clashes becomes a Conflict.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "room_blocked_b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Blocked times. An approver of a room can keep the room free, for example for repairs or a holiday. Add a Room Booking with the status Blocked. It needs no Requester. A request for a blocked time is refused, also with Request Anyway ticked. When you save a blocked time, each Requested or Conflict booking at that time is denied. An Approved booking at that time refuses the blocked time: cancel or move it first. Only an approver of the room can add, change or remove a blocked time.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "room_equip_b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Equipment. To let people book a Church Asset, such as a projector or the van, open it and tick Bookable. On a Room Booking, choose the equipment in Equipment. You can leave Room empty to book equipment only. A booking of equipment only is Approved at once and belongs to your church. Equipment can be in only one booking at a time, and a Conflict booking keeps its equipment too. If another booking has the equipment at that time, the booking is refused and the message names the other booking. If that booking belongs to a church you cannot see, the message only counts it.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "room_loan_b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Lend equipment. Use a Room Booking to lend equipment. Add the equipment to Equipment and leave Room empty. A booking of equipment only is Approved at once.
1. When the borrower takes the equipment, open the booking and click Check Out. Checked Out On shows the time.
2. When the borrower brings the equipment back, open the booking and click Check In. Returned On shows the time, and the status changes to Completed.
Only a Church Manager can check equipment out or in. Nobody can type these times by hand. You cannot check out equipment that is still out on another booking: check in that booking first. A Completed booking does not hold its room or its equipment, so other people can book them again. The Assets on Loan report shows all equipment that is out and not returned. The booking with the oldest End is at the top, so late returns show first.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "room_function_b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Rooms for a Function. To book rooms for a Function, open the Function and click Create, then Book a Room. Choose one or more rooms and any equipment, check the Requester and the times, and click Book. Each room gets its own booking, and the equipment goes with the first booking that saves. Book a Room does not show a room that has a Question Set. Book that room on its own Room Booking form.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "room_calendar_b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Room calendar. Click Room Calendar in the Operations sidebar to see the room bookings by month, week or day. The calendar does not show Denied and Cancelled bookings. Remove the Status filter to see them. The Room Booking list has the same filter. Click a booking to open it. You see the bookings of your churches and the bookings of shared rooms.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "room_request_b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Room requests from members. Members ask for a room on the Book a Room page of the member portal (/room-request). A member chooses a room, the start, the end and the purpose, and can add notes. The page offers only the bookable rooms of the member's church and the shared rooms. The member is always the Requester of the booking. On a room with Requires Approval ticked, the request stays Requested until an approver approves it. The member sees only their own requests and their status. The Room Request form does not show a room that has a required question. Staff book that room on the Room Booking form. Members cannot book equipment. Staff add it to the booking. A visitor who is not signed in must log in first. If your portal menu does not have Book a Room, open Portal Settings and add a row to Menu with the Title Book a Room, the Route room-request, the Reference Document Type Room Booking and the Role Church User.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "room_sheet_b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Setup sheets. To give the people who set up a room what they need, open the Room Booking, click Print and choose Setup Sheet. The sheet shows the room, the start and end times, the purpose and the requester, the setup with its capacity and description, the setup notes, the equipment and the answers to the room's questions. Print it or click Get PDF.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "room_usage_b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Room Usage report. To see how your rooms and equipment are used, open the Room Usage report (Operations Reports in the Operations sidebar). It shows one row for each booking whose times are in the dates you choose: the room, the equipment, the start and end, the hours, the status, the requester and the purpose. You can show only one room or one status. The report shows the bookings of your churches and the bookings of shared rooms. Church Managers and Church Staff can open it.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "room_church_b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Rooms with more than one church. A room belongs to one church, and only that church can book it. Tick Shared with all churches on a room to let every church book it. A shared room has one diary for every church, so every church sees its bookings and a booking blocks that time for all of them. The Requester of a booking must be a person of the church that books the room.", "col": 12}}]
